name: Rami J. Elkhechen
headline: Sports medicine orthopedic surgeon

affiliation.name: NYU Langone Medical Associates, Palm Beach Gardens

on_the_show: Dr. Elkhechen talked with Dave and Mike about what separates a surgical candidate from someone better served by conservative care, and why he tries non-operative treatment as often as he can first. He described cartilage as “the gold in a vault at a bank,” with the ligaments and meniscus as its security system, and walked through cartilage restoration and the rehab after it. He also does prehab before surgery, especially for ACL patients, because a stronger base going in means a better recovery coming out.

background.text: He is a Clinical Assistant Professor in the Department of Orthopedic Surgery at NYU Grossman School of Medicine and sees patients at NYU Langone Medical Associates in Palm Beach Gardens.
He earned his medical degree at New York University and completed his orthopedic surgery residency at SUNY Downstate in Brooklyn.
He completed a sports medicine fellowship at the Ochsner Clinic Foundation in New Orleans.
During his fellowship he served as an assistant team physician for the New Orleans Saints and New Orleans Pelicans.
He is board certified by the American Board of Orthopaedic Surgery.
His practice covers sports medicine and arthroscopic surgery of the shoulder, elbow, hip, knee and ankle, including cartilage procedures and ACL reconstruction.
